For page-level density analysis, use the keyword density tool, which computes from the full-text word frequencies.
map.不是。适度的关键词密度有助于主题识别，但过高（堆砌）会损害可读性、甚至被搜索引擎: No. A moderate keyword density helps topic identification, but too high a density (keyword stuffing) harms readability and may even be judged as cheating by search engines. The max and the range from this tool help you locate outlier drafts, but whether the final density is reasonable must be judged against the genre (a press release is usually far below an SEO landing page).
map.公关稿发稿前，统计核心关键词在各篇稿件中的出现频次，做描述统计看密度是否均匀、有: Before publishing a PR article, count the frequency of the core keywords across the articles and run descriptive statistics to see whether the density is even and whether any article is stuffed.

map.：8 篇新闻稿中「绿色低碳」一词出现次数 10、20、30、40、50、60、7: : The term "green and low-carbon" appears 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 times across 8 press releases: n = 8, sum 360.00, mean 45.00, median 45.00, minimum 10, maximum 80, range 70.00, variance 525.00, standard deviation 22.91. The mean of 45 per article represents the average density; the range of 70 shows the articles differ sharply, and if one article reaches 80 while most others are in the 10 to 50 range, that article is likely deliberately stuffed, so its readability should be reviewed by hand to avoid triggering a search engine over-optimization verdict.
map.：样本量 n；总和；算术均值 = 总和 ÷ n；中位数；最小值、最大值与极差；方: : Count n; sum; arithmetic mean = sum ÷ n; median; minimum, maximum, and range; variance = Σ(x − mean)² ÷ n (population basis); standard deviation = √variance. The input is the number of occurrences of a keyword in each article (separated by commas, spaces, or newlines).
